decided_by: w7-integration for David (fix list A1, card 2026-10-24)
basis: Fix list A1 carried through S14: S13 holds a net product-tax rate on every cell (tax_cells_s13.csv.gz; the pet, coa, gas and ely rows at the S10 energy-tax rates; since QA round 2 P1 the non-energy rows at their commodity rates from S13 non_energy_rates, else one rate), the same on domestic and imported purchases. S14 keeps those cell rates (as wedges over the column's median non-energy rate) and sets one remainder rate per column (that median, up to rounding) so the column tax equals its io_s13 TLS and PSE_input over its basic purchases; in a column the A13 seed moves, the remainder is re-set to hold the column's tax, so every cell there is its S13 rate plus one shift. GTAP 12 ch.12 books energy taxes on the energy rows; ch.2 Table 2.3 holds rates by commodity, source and agent. S14-Hpower (one power per cell; on the non-energy rows the S13 rates plus one shift per column) and S14-Hcellrates (every cell at its S13 rate) check it. one_tax_power_per_column_dom_and_imp_from_s13 is the pre-fix-round alternative (it would undo A1).
ACTS = COMM in the Julia port (model_requirements §1a); MAKB is output at basic prices and MAKS = MAKB less the output tax (PTAX, including farm output support), as PLAN §3(j) writes it.

GTAP 12 ch.17B §B.2: re-balancing corrects imbalances between supply and usage and between income and disposition. Upstream files are rounded to 1e-6 USD million, so S14 makes VCIF = VFOB + VTWR per route, world VST = world VTWR, imports = VMSB, output = sales and zero profit exact. Each move is at most 1e-3 USD million (S14-Hrebalance); anything larger is not rounding and fails (PLAN §3(i) no plugs).

David chose report-only in the S14 thread (2026-10-24 10:24 UTC+7), on the card after QA C1: trade-data causes are fixed upstream, genuine ones stay as GTAP allows. PLAN §3(h)3 and E12 ask for SAVE > 0 or a cited cause. GTAP 12 ch.7 eq. 7.1 makes SAVE a residual that may be negative, and the only cause S14 can state from the data restates that identity, so a cause row would pass every region by construction. SAVE <= 0 is report-only (flag NEG-SAVE) with the eq. 7.2 BoP memo and the trade balance against S02 national-accounts NX beside it (screen 1). hard_save_positive stops the stamp on any SAVE <= 0.

Fix list B14 (QA#17): about 118 thousand VXSB routes and 454 thousand VTWR cells are below USD 1 (1e-6 USD million). Before the re-balancing and before the A13 seed, a route with VXSB below USD 1 is dropped with its border values and margins, and a VTWR cell below USD 1 is set to zero (VCIF falls by it; VMSB keeps its tariff power). Tiny cells add nothing and slow the solves. A filter at this size is our choice: GTAP filters small values, but its threshold is not in the documents we hold. Ledger rule 'B14 trade cells below USD 1 set to zero'; the cells are listed in small_trade_s14.csv.gz. keep_all turns it off.

Fix list A13 (David 2026-10-24): the 332 commodity-region pairs bought only from imports get a small domestic supply before the balance, as GTAP 10 has none (every bought commodity has some domestic purchase there). Size (our choice): every column that buys the import buys 1e-4 of that purchase from domestic producers, inside the 1e-6 to 1e-3 range David gave. Closure (our choice): the column gives up the same basic value of its other purchases pro rata, at most half of them (fix round w17, URY mvh: the rest of the row's seed goes to the other buyers pro rata to their imports, so the row seed stays exact and no cell turns negative), the imports given up become the new activity's imported inputs, and each supplying activity hands the matching share of its whole column (inputs, product taxes, factor payments, output tax) to the new activity, so its cost structure is the region's own supplying columns (land carved from a land-using supplier is paid as capital in a new activity that uses no land, fix round S16, so land stays in the activities GTAP gives it) and every market, cost, factor, tax, C, G, I, X, M and GDP total stays exact. Ledger rules 'A13 seed domestic supply in a one-sided pair' and 'A13 seed cost structure carved from the supplying columns'; the pairs are listed in seeded_pairs_s14.csv. The other side (fix round, S15 smoke map): the 31 pairs bought only from domestic producers (crude in 30 exporters once A8 sends crude only to refining, msp in GIN) import 1e-4 of their domestic purchases through a tax-free, margin-free swap with a partner exporter (two new routes of the same size; both regions switch that much of their domestic purchases to imports, so every total stays); our choice, rule 'A13 seed imports in a domestic-only pair', listed in swapped_pairs_s14.csv. none turns it off (S16 then needs its fuel-pooling schemes back).

Fix list B16 (David's card 2026-10-24 14:13 UTC, "GTAP rule in all resource sectors"; standing rule "stick to GTAP", 2026-10-24 14:44 UTC). GTAP 12 ch.17B §B.1 places the reallocation of labour and capital earnings to natural resources (target supply elasticities, GTAP 7 ch.12.A pp.2-3) in the global data assembly after the FIT, so it holds on the final data. S12 sets the share at its prior theta_VA; S13 holds each factor's share of VA but moves VA over output, so S14 sets it again at its own theta_VA = sum EVFP / MAKS with S12's targets, sigma_VA (config/s12/natres_targets.csv) and guard (S12 natres_guard): eta = sigma_VA (1/theta_R - 1/theta_VA) equals the target. Labour and capital give or take the difference pro rata, each cell at its own factor-use and income-tax rates; natural resources keep theirs (no factor-use tax and capital's income-tax rate where the region has none, as S12). Column VA, cost, output tax and regional income are unchanged. Hard checks S14-Heta, S14-Hnatpro, S14-Hnatcfg; reports S14-Rnatguard, S14-Rnatres. as_s13_s12_prior_shares keeps factors_s13's split (eta at the target only at the S12 prior).

decided_by: Claude (beta v4 fixes thread) at the S16 thread's request
basis: Beta v4, S16 alone_bfa: BFA coal, an A13 seed column of 7e-9 USD million from about USD 76 of travel coal imports, had capital of 8e-10 and calibrated with VA and zero capital. Two steps, both labelled departures. (1) An A13 seed is at least 1e-5 USD million (USD 10), at most half the row's imports (the row's seed ratio rises above 1e-4; where the buyers cannot give that up, the plain 1e-4 stands). (2) After B16, every activity with value added pays capital of at least min(1e-6 USD million, half its VA), taken from its labour pro rata (EVFP, EVFB and EVOS alike): column VA, factor-tax money and regional income are unchanged, land and natural resources are untouched. Thresholds are our choice; GTAP 12 has no capital minimum (GTAP filters small values; its threshold is not in the documents we hold). Alternative off: the plain 1e-4 seed and no floor.
